causes.label: The door was opened or the cycle was interrupted.
remedies: Press the Start pad once and close the door within 4 seconds to start the dishwasher.
Press the Start pad a second time when the dishwasher is running only if you wish to cancel the cycle.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "The door was opened or the cycle was interrupted."

causes.label: This is a reminder that your dishwasher door has been left open during operation. It will continue beeping until you press Start and close the door.
remedies: Press Start and close the door.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "This is a reminder that your dishwasher door has been left open during operation. It will continue beeping until you press Start and close the door."

symptoms.symptom: Beeping at the end of the cycle

causes.label: This is normal. Dishwasher will beep at end of cycle.
remedies: The dishwasher will beep (unless interupted) and the Clean light will display at the end of the wash cycle.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "This is normal. Dishwasher will beep at end of cycle."

causes.label: Filter assembly is clogged
remedies: See the CARE AND CLEANING section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Filter assembly is clogged"

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure inlet water temperature is correct (see the USING THE DISHWASHER section).
Turn on the hot water faucet nearest the dishwasher, let run until the water temperature stops rising.
Then start the dishwasher and turn off the faucet.
This ensures the entering water is hot.
Select Wash Temp - Boost.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Low inlet water temperature"

causes.label: Water pressure is temporarily low
remedies: Turn on a faucet.
Is water coming out more slowly than usual?
If so, wait until pressure is normal before using your dishwasher.
Normal water pressure to the dishwasher should be 20-120 psi.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Water pressure is temporarily low"

causes.label: High drain loop or air gap not installed (Built-In Models Only)
remedies: Refer to the Installation Instructions for proper drain line installation.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "High drain loop or air gap not installed (Built-In Models Only)"

causes.label: Improper rack loading
remedies: Make sure large dishware or utensils do not block detergent dispenser or the wash arms.
See the Loading section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Improper rack loading"

causes.label: Poor performing detergent
remedies: Use high quality detergents such as Cascade® Platinum™ ActionPacs™ or Finish® Quantum® Automatic Dishwashing Detergent.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Poor performing detergent"

symptoms.symptom: Spots and filming on glasses and flatware

causes.label: Extremely hard water
remedies: se high quality rinse agents such as Cascade® Platinum™ Power Dry™ Rinse Aid or Finish® Jet-Dry® Rinse Aid to prevent spots and prevent new film build-up.
If water is extremely hard, a softener may be required.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Extremely hard water"

causes.label: Low inlet water temperature
remedies: Make sure inlet water temperature is at least 120°F (49°C).
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Low inlet water temperature"

causes.label: Overloading or improper loading of the dishwasher
remedies: Load dishwasher as shown in the Loading section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Overloading or improper loading of the dishwasher"

causes.label: Old or damp powder detergent
remedies: Make sure detergent is fresh.
Use high quality detergents such as Cascade® Platinum™ ActionPacs™ or Finish® Quantum® Automatic Dishwashing Detergent.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Old or damp powder detergent"

causes.label: Rinse agent dispenser empty
remedies: Refill with high quality rinse agents such as Cascade® Platinum™ Power Dry™ Rinse Aid or Finish® Jet-Dry® Rinse Aid.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Rinse agent dispenser empty"

causes.label: Too little or low performing detergent
remedies: Make sure you use the proper amount of highly rated detergent.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Too little or low performing detergent"

causes.label: Combination of soft water and too much detergent
remedies: This is called etching and is permanent.
To prevent this from happening, use less detergent if you have soft water.
Wash glassware in the shortest cycle that will get it clean.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 16: "Combination of soft water and too much detergent"

causes.label: Wrong detergent
remedies: Use only high quality automatic dishwasher detergents to avoid sudsing.
Cascade® Platinum™ ActionPacs™ or Finish® Quantum® Automatic Dishwashing Detergent have been approved for use in all GE Appliances dishwashers.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 17: "Wrong detergent"

causes.label: Rinse agent was spilled
remedies: Always wipe up rinse agent spills immediately.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 17: "Rinse agent was spilled"

causes.label: Dishes or utensils are blocking the detergent cup
remedies: Reposition the dishes, so the water from the lower spray arm can flush the detergent cup.
See the Loading section.
Reposition the tall utensils or heavy silverware that may be keeping the dispenser cup door from opening.
See the Loading section.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 17: "Dishes or utensils are blocking the detergent cup"

causes.evidence: GE manual, page 17: "Door not opened immediately after Clean light came on"

remedies: Make sure inlet water temperature is at least 120°F.
Use Wash Temp Boost.

causes.label: Rinse agent dispenser is empty

causes.evidence: GE manual, page 17: "Rinse agent dispenser is empty"

remedies: A special filter in the water supply line is the only way to correct this problem.
Contact a water softener company.

causes.label: White film on inside surface— hard water minerals
remedies: GE Appliances recommends high quality rinse agents such as Cascade® Platinum™ Power Dry™ Rinse Aid or Finish® Jet-Dry® Rinse Aid to help prevent hard water mineral deposits from forming.
Run dishwasher with citric acid to remove mineral deposits.
Citric acid (Part number: WD35X151) can be ordered through GE Appliances Parts.
See back cover for ordering information.
Alternatively, purchase Cascade® Platinum™ Dishwasher Cleaner or Finish® Dishwasher Cleaner and follow the directions on the label.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 17: "White film on inside surface— hard water minerals"

causes.label: Fuse is blown or circuit breaker is tripped
remedies: Replace fuse or reset circuit breaker.
Remove any other appliances from the circuit.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 17: "Fuse is blown or circuit breaker is tripped"

causes.label: Power is turned off
remedies: In some installations, the power to the dishwasher is provided through a wall switch, often located next to the disposer switch.
Make sure it is on.

causes.evidence: GE manual, page 17: "Reboot your control"

symptoms.symptom: A white film on glassware, dishware and the interior Forget to Add a Dish?

causes.label: This problem is likely caused by a low quality phosphate-free dishwasher detergent
remedies: To remove the white film, run your dishes through a dishwasher cycle with citric acid.
Use a WD35X151 citric acid kit found online.
Otherwise, use high quality rinse agents such as Cascade® Platinum™ Dishwasher Cleaner or Finish® Dishwasher Cleaner found at your local grocery store.
Pour the citric acid in the detergent cup and close the cover.
Place the filmed but otherwise clean glassware and dishware in the dishwasher.
Leave silverware and other metal items out of the dishwasher.
Turn the dishwasher on and let it run through a complete cycle without detergent.
The glassware, dishware, and dishwasher should come out film free.
Alternatively, a vinegar rinse may be used.
Pour 1 cup of vinegar into dishwasher just after the detergent cup opens and let the dishwasher complete its cycle.
This may be repeated several times a year as needed.
The use of high quality rinse agents such as Cascade® Platinum™ Power Dry™ Rinse Aid or Finish® Jet-Dry® Rinse Aid may help minimize a repeat build up of film.
Also, the use of high quality detergents such as Cascade® Platinum™ ActionPacs™ or Finish® Quantum® Automatic Dishwashing Detergent will help prevent film build-up.
causes.evidence: GE manual, page 18: "This problem is likely caused by a low quality phosphate-free dishwasher detergent"
